findings: Before: 15/16 common fixture matches; added-source times out for both
After: 8/16 common fixture matches; 6 common operation deadlines and 2 common readiness deadlines
No asymmetric path/deadline-category outcome in either paired cohort
Shared operation failures occur after both subscriptions acknowledge the same readiness file
limitations: Concurrent paired subscriptions are an intervention; not an uninstrumented acceptance gate
Go diagnostic selects PythonSource to observe identical .py paths; does not exercise CLI GoSource filename adaptation
The full-suite preload may affect shared filesystem/daemon state but causality is unproven; no randomized/reversed/isolated workload comparison
Readiness probe deadlines are 5s, operation deadlines 3s; outer JSON/process coordination waits use 8s; not identical to every original caller arming budget
Source filtered/delivered paths and Go batches are observed; this experiment does not trace raw Source/Go C callbacks
Known IDNA failures, full native reliability, default diagnostics and complete G0-G7 remain open
Go starts a fresh process for each case, while Source reuses one Python process per 16-case cohort; registration history is not fully matched
cleanup: Both control processes exited 0 after all 16 cases; all 32 Go probes exited 0 and Close acknowledgments returned without error. Source workers joined in both scripts; successful operations record source_closed, while two readiness-failure rows rely on the finally cleanup execution path. No independent Source native __exit__ counter is claimed.
